Since L≥2, there is an unchanged strictly positive interior weight, even at the corner where both variable endpoint weights vanish. With the mean strictly between 0 and L, increasing the 0 weight decreases it and increasing the L weight increases it. The extrema are the claimed opposing corners; connectedness and continuity give the full interval.

Write the two means on indices 0 through L−1. The shifted law with weights w_(i+1) has mean m_+−1 and the unshifted law has mean m_−. Cross multiplication gives a double sum with coefficient j−i; grouping the (i,j) and (j,i) terms gives the displayed identity.
For i<j, adjacent log-concavity and positivity imply w_(j+1)/w_j≤w_(i+1)/w_i, so each grouped term is nonpositive. For constant weights the means are (L−1)/2 and (L+1)/2, including L=2.
